info.title: PDFBolt API
info.summary: PDF generation and reusable template management API
info.description:
PDFBolt provides REST APIs for generating PDFs from Base64-encoded HTML,
HTTPS URLs, and published templates with JSON data, and for managing reusable templates.

The Conversion API has three modes:
Direct returns the generated PDF in the HTTP response, Sync returns a
temporary download URL, and Async accepts a background job and delivers the
final result to your webhook.

The Template API lets
you create and manage reusable templates programmatically using a
Personal Access Token.

Outbound URL fetching, webhook delivery, and custom S3 uploads use PDFBolt's
static outbound IP addresses. See [IP Addresses](https://pdfbolt.com/docs/ip-addresses).

Open the raw OpenAPI YAML: [openapi.yaml](/openapi.yaml).

post.summary: Generate a PDF and return it in the response body
post.description:
Generates a PDF from a URL, Base64-encoded HTML, or a published template
ID with template data, then returns the generated document directly in
the HTTP response body. Use this endpoint when your application needs the
PDF immediately.

encoded.summary: Return the PDF as Base64 text

200.description: Generated PDF returned as binary PDF or Base64-encoded text.

post.summary: Generate a PDF and return a temporary download URL
post.description:
Generates a PDF from a URL, Base64-encoded HTML, or a published template
ID with template data, then returns a JSON response with a downloadable
document URL. By default, files stored in PDFBolt's temporary storage
expire after 24 hours. You can provide `customS3PresignedUrl` to upload
the PDF directly to your own S3-compatible bucket.

url.summary: Convert a URL to PDF and receive a download URL

html.summary: Convert Base64 HTML to PDF and receive a download URL

template.summary: Convert a template to PDF and receive a download URL

customS3.summary: Upload the generated PDF to a custom S3-compatible bucket

200.description: PDF generated successfully. The response contains the conversion result.

post.summary: Generate a PDF and deliver the result by webhook
post.description:
Generates a PDF in the background, immediately returns a `requestId`, and
delivers the final result to your HTTPS webhook URL once the job succeeds
or permanently fails. The `webhook` parameter is required. You can provide
`customS3PresignedUrl` to upload the PDF directly to your own
S3-compatible bucket. This endpoint is available on paid plans.

url.summary: Generate a PDF from a URL and receive the result by webhook

html.summary: Generate a PDF from Base64 HTML and receive the result by webhook

template.summary: Generate a PDF from a template and receive the result by webhook

customS3.summary: Generate a PDF from a URL and upload it to a custom S3-compatible bucket

200.description: Async request accepted for background processing.

get.summary: Get current plan and remaining conversions
get.description:
Returns the authenticated account's current plan, recurring conversion
details, one-time conversion packages, remaining conversions, overage,
and expiration dates. Use the same `API-KEY` header as the Conversion API
endpoints. Use it to track conversion usage, not API request limits.

Returns the current Template Contract. It covers supported fields, defaults, rendering guidance, limits, errors, and the recommended workflow for creating and publishing templates. Use it for PDFBolt-specific template rules and this OpenAPI document for exact request and response schemas. No authentication is required.

head.summary: Check the public Template Contract endpoint
head.description: Returns the same status and response headers as GET /v1/templates/contract without a response body. No authentication is required.

200.description: Template Contract endpoint is available. The response has no body.

503.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. The response has no body.

get.description: Returns the current team's templates with published and draft version details, excluding deleted templates. Results are ordered by the latest version update, newest first, and are not paginated.

Returns details for the template identified by `templateId`, including its content, sample data, PDF parameters, and metadata for the active draft and latest published version. If an active draft exists, the content, sample data, and PDF parameters come from it. Otherwise, they come from the latest published version.

delete.description: Removes the entire template from the team's active templates. Its draft and published versions can no longer be accessed through the Template API or used for new conversions. This API does not provide a restore operation. Already generated PDFs are unaffected, and a conversion that has already loaded the template may finish. Returns 404 for missing, previously deleted, or another team's templates. Does not consume conversion credits. Management rate limits apply.

post.description: Validates a template payload without saving it or rendering a PDF. It checks required fields, Base64 content, payload size limits, the template engine, Handlebars syntax and evaluation, and supported PDF parameters. Handlebars placeholders without matching values in `sampleData` render as empty text and do not cause validation to fail. Use it before previewing or saving a draft.
Renders a template payload as a PDF without saving it as a template or draft. Each successful preview render counts toward your available document conversions.

parameters.name: responseFormat
parameters.description: Response format. Defaults to `url`, which returns a temporary `documentUrl`, `expiresAt`, and `documentSizeMb`. Use `pdf` to return raw PDF bytes or `json` to return `pdfBase64` and `documentSizeMb`. Every format returns the conversion cost in the `x-pdfbolt-conversion-cost` response header.

post.summary: Compare proposed changes with the published version
post.description: The template must have a published version. The endpoint renders the published version as `before` and the supplied template payload as `after` for visual comparison without saving the changes. The conversion cost is calculated separately for each successfully rendered side.

parameters.name: responseFormat
parameters.description: Response format. Defaults to `url`, which returns temporary `documentUrl` and `expiresAt` values. Use `json` to return each rendered PDF as `pdfBase64` instead. Both formats include `documentSizeMb` and `error` for each side and report the conversion cost in the `x-pdfbolt-conversion-cost` response header.

200.description: Comparison completed. Rendering failures are returned in `before.error` or `after.error` while the response remains HTTP 200.

post.summary: Create or update a template draft
post.description: Creates a new template and its first draft when `templateId` is omitted. When `templateId` is provided, the endpoint updates only the supplied fields, using the active draft as the base or the published version if no active draft exists. Supplied `content` and `sampleData` replace their complete stored values. For `parameters`, only the fields you provide are updated. Every save validates the complete draft, including fields preserved during an update, without rendering a PDF or consuming conversion credits.

Publishes the template's active draft. You can then generate PDFs from the published template by sending its `templateId` and `templateData` to a Conversion API endpoint. Wait for any save request for this template to finish before publishing it.

PDFBolt sends this webhook to the URL provided in the `webhook`
parameter of an async conversion request. PDFBolt attempts one callback
for each accepted async conversion: after the conversion succeeds or
after all configured conversion retries fail. Verify the
`x-pdfbolt-signature` header with your webhook signature key before
trusting the payload.

parameters.name: x-pdfbolt-signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw webhook request body, prefixed with `sha256=` and encoded as lowercase hex. Verify the exact bytes received in the HTTP body before parsing or re-serializing JSON.

parameters.name: x-pdfbolt-conversion-cost
parameters.description: Number of document credits charged for the conversion. For failed conversions, PDFBolt sends `0`.

2XX.description: Your webhook endpoint should return a successful 2xx response after accepting the callback.

apiKeyAuth.name: API-KEY
apiKeyAuth.description: API key from the API Credentials page in the PDFBolt Dashboard

personalAccessTokenAuth.name: PERSONAL-ACCESS-TOKEN
personalAccessTokenAuth.description: Personal Access Token from the API Credentials page in the PDFBolt Dashboard. Used by Template API endpoints.

ConversionCost.description: Document credits charged for the request.

ContentDisposition.description: Controls inline vs attachment delivery and includes a filename when provided.

RateLimitMinute.description: Request limit for the current rolling minute.

RateLimitRemainingMinute.description: Requests remaining in the current rolling minute.

RateLimitHour.description: Request limit for the current rolling hour.

RateLimitRemainingHour.description: Requests remaining in the current rolling hour.

RateLimitDay.description: Request limit for the current rolling 24-hour window.

RateLimitRemainingDay.description: Requests remaining in the current rolling 24-hour window.

RetryAfter.description: Approximate number of whole seconds until a slot becomes available in the rolling window that rejected the request. Fractional seconds are rounded up.

Accept.description: Media types supported for the request body.

BadRequest.description: Invalid JSON, invalid parameter values, or a problem with the conversion source.

SyncBadRequest.description: Invalid JSON, invalid parameter values, a problem with the conversion source, or a custom S3 upload error.

AsyncBadRequest.description: Invalid JSON, invalid field types, or invalid parameter values.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication failed because the API key is missing, invalid, or blocked.

Forbidden.description: The API key is valid, but the account cannot perform this action.

NotFound.description: The requested API endpoint could not be found.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request payload or generated PDF exceeds the allowed size.

RequestPayloadTooLarge.description: The request payload exceeds the allowed size.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The request could not be processed correctly.

TooManyRequests.description: The account exceeded minute, hour, day, or concurrent request limits.

TemplateApiUnsupportedMediaType.description: The request's `Content-Type` is not supported by this endpoint.

TemplateApiRenderingUnsupportedMediaType.description: The request's `Content-Type` is not supported by this endpoint.

TemplateApiPublishBadRequest.description: The request is invalid or the template has no active draft to publish.

TemplateApiSaveDraftBadRequest.description: The request body is malformed or the draft payload failed validation.

TemplateApiValidateBadRequest.description: The request body is malformed or the template payload failed validation. Check the required fields, Base64 content, `sampleData`, the template engine, Handlebars syntax and evaluation, and PDF parameters.

TemplateApiInvalidIdBadRequest.description: The `templateId` path parameter is not a valid UUID.

TemplateApiPreviewBadRequest.description: The request body is malformed, `responseFormat` is unsupported, the template payload failed validation, or PDF rendering failed before the preview could be returned.

TemplateApiDiffBadRequest.description: The `templateId` path parameter is invalid, `responseFormat` is unsupported, the request body is malformed, or template validation failed before rendering.

TemplateApiUnauthorized.description: Authentication failed because the Personal Access Token is missing, invalid, inactive, or blocked.

TemplateApiTemplateLimitForbidden.description: A new template could not be created because your team has reached the template limit for its current plan.

TemplateApiConversionForbidden.description: The preview could not be rendered because PDF conversion is unavailable.

TemplateApiNotFound.description: The template does not exist or does not belong to your current team.

TemplateApiDiffNotFound.description: The template does not exist, does not belong to your current team, or has no published version.

TemplateApiPayloadTooLarge.description: One of `content`, `sampleData`, or `parameters` exceeds its size limit.

TemplateApiPublishPayloadTooLarge.description: One of the active draft fields (`content`, `sampleData`, or `parameters`) exceeds its size limit.

TemplateApiValidatePayloadTooLarge.description: The request exceeds the applicable size limit for decoded HTML content, `sampleData`, or `parameters`.

TemplateApiDiffPayloadTooLarge.description: One of `content`, `sampleData`, or `parameters` exceeds its size limit before rendering.

TemplateApiPreviewPayloadTooLarge.description: The template payload or generated preview PDF exceeds the applicable size limit.

TemplateApiUnprocessableEntity.description: The request could not be processed correctly.

TemplateApiTooManyRequests.description: You have exceeded a Template API management rate limit. See [Rate Limits](https://pdfbolt.com/docs/rate-limits) for current limits.

ClientDisconnected.description: PDFBolt detected that the client disconnected before the response could be fully delivered. The standard JSON body is documented for consistency, but the client will not receive it if the connection is already closed.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Service temporarily unavailable. Infrastructure-generated responses may not follow PDFBolt's standard JSON error format.

GatewayTimeout.description: Gateway timeout. Infrastructure-generated responses may not follow PDFBolt's standard JSON error format.

timestamp.description: Date and time when the error occurred.

httpErrorCode.description: HTTP status code of the error.

templateData.description: Only used with `templateId`. JSON data used to fill variables in the published template.

isEncoded.description: When `true`, returns the generated PDF as Base64 text instead of binary PDF.

javaScriptEnabled.description: Whether JavaScript execution is enabled while rendering the source content.

isMobile.description: Enables mobile device emulation, including mobile viewport behavior and touch events.

deviceScaleFactor.description: Pixel density used when rendering the page. Higher values can produce sharper output.

extraHTTPHeaders.description: Custom HTTP headers sent while PDFBolt loads the source content and page resources. Maximum 10 headers.

applyExtraHTTPHeadersToAllResources.description: Whether `extraHTTPHeaders` are sent with all resource requests or only with the main page request.

cookies.description: Cookies sent while rendering the source content. Each cookie must include name, value, and either url or both domain and path. Optional fields are expires, httpOnly, and secure. Maximum 10 cookies.

waitForFunction.description: JavaScript function evaluated in the page context. PDF generation continues when it returns true.

timeout.description: Maximum render wait time in milliseconds. The allowed maximum depends on your plan.

landscape.description: Page orientation for the generated PDF.

width.description: Custom page width for the generated PDF. Used when format is not provided. Accepts a number of pixels or a string with px, in, cm, or mm units.

height.description: Custom page height for the generated PDF. Used when format is not provided. Accepts a number of pixels or a string with px, in, cm, or mm units.

pageRanges.description: Comma-separated page ranges such as `1-3,5,8-11`. Omit to include all pages.

preferCssPageSize.description: Whether to use the CSS `@page` size when generating the PDF.

printBackground.description: Whether to include CSS background colors, gradients, and images.

scale.description: Scaling factor for rendering the content in the generated PDF.

displayHeaderFooter.description: Whether to render the `headerTemplate` and `footerTemplate` content in the generated PDF.

headerTemplate.description: Base64-encoded HTML for the page header. Used when `displayHeaderFooter` is `true`. Available classes: `pageNumber`, `totalPages`, `title`, `url`, `date`.

footerTemplate.description: Base64-encoded HTML for the page footer. Used when `displayHeaderFooter` is `true`. Available classes: `pageNumber`, `totalPages`, `title`, `url`, `date`.

tagged.description: Whether to generate a tagged PDF with structural information for accessibility tools.

filename.description:
Filename embedded in the `Content-Disposition` header. Allowed
characters are letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens. If
`.pdf` is omitted, PDFBolt adds it automatically.

example.description: Default PDF options saved on template versions. When creating a template with POST /v1/templates/drafts, PDFBolt starts from the same defaults as the Dashboard designer: format=Letter, landscape=false, waitUntil=load, printBackground=true, displayHeaderFooter=false, headerTemplate omitted, footerTemplate omitted and a standard readiness waitForFunction. Any provided parameter field overrides that default. When updating an existing template, parameters is a shallow patch against the active draft, or the published version when no draft exists. Omit parameters to preserve every option. An empty {} also preserves every option but must accompany another changed top-level field. For save, validate, preview and diff, null headerTemplate, footerTemplate or waitForFunction removes that option from the effective parameters; during an update this unsets a saved value. Null format, landscape, waitUntil, printBackground or displayHeaderFooter is invalid.

example.description: Short internal description. When creating a template, an omitted or null description is stored as an empty string. When updating a draft, omit it to preserve the current description, send an empty string to clear it, or provide a string; null is invalid.

example.description: Base64-encoded complete HTML document with CSS. Required for validate, preview, diff and new draft creation. For an existing draft update, omit it to preserve the current document or provide a value to replace the complete document; null is invalid.

example.description: JSON object used to evaluate the Handlebars template. Required for validate, preview, diff and new draft creation. For an existing draft update, omit it to preserve the current object, provide an object to replace it, or send {} to clear it; null is invalid.

example.name: parameters
example.description: Template default options. Required for validate, preview and diff. Optional when creating a template; missing fields use template creation defaults. For an existing draft update, this is a shallow patch: omitted fields are preserved and null is invalid for the parameters object itself. Sending only templateId and parameters={} is rejected because it changes nothing; {} is valid alongside another changed top-level field.
